title: Tommy Miles's band when Phillips arrived: Mundy, Tyree Glenn, Jefferson
summary: Phillips lists the 1935 personnel of Tommy Miles's band and Jimmy Mundy's arrangements such as Cavernism.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Who was in Tommy Miles band when you first heard him?
The band I got in with Tommy was a new band.
Yeah, I know. But when you first came in to town, in '35?
He had Warren Jefferson, Tyree Glenn, Jimmy Mundy...
What was Jimmy Mundy doing?
He was gone. He just had left, and went with...
He'd done some arranging for the band, hadn't he, before he left?
He played. He played tenor.
Did he arrange too?
Yeah.
Were any of his charts still in the band at that time?
Yeah. "Cavernism" -- that was one of his tunes. He's arranging somewhere out in California now. He's
Phillips - 171
arranging for some of them studios. He's big-time now.
Anybody else who was in the band when you first came in? Who was playing drums and bass?

Tommy was the drummer. Benny Fonville was the bassist. I'm trying to think of this guitar player's name. Hell of a guitar player. Wiley(?) Duke. He died. Jimmy Homes playing guitar. I told you Benny Fonville was on bass, Tommy was on drums. John Thompson was playing the piano.
This was in '35, when you first got to D.C.

Yeah. Paul Jones was playing tenor. That's the cat I told you about who wanted to get Les, and Les blew him out the hall. Buster... We called him Buster McPherson -- he was playing first alto. Doc Washington was playing third alto. He was a doctor, we called him Doc. He's practicing now, he's a dentist. He quit playing. He was going to college then and playing. That was it.
That's a pretty good memory.
I didn't name the trumpet players, though. Jeff -- Warren Jefferson. Leon Hill was playing trumpet. That was all the trumpets. Wendell Jackson was playing the other trombone. That was it.
